investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that advertise it. When the eval runner called createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764), the resulting pod could not be scheduled: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for ~149 s until the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots and they have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peerpods nodes), and those 2 nodes are at capacity — any change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec could cause this split.

Cluster under-provisioned for the remote-agent workload: only 2 nodes are configured to support kata.peerpods.io/vm, which may be insufficient if multiple concurrent eval runs or user workloads compete for the same resource.

Leaked or zombie VM allocations from previous eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if prior probe runs failed before cleanup executed, their VM slots may still be held, reducing available capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create that produces a scheduled pod and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would disprove that the resource is currently exhausted.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and no pods currently consuming those slots would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike) rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., a label change on the 2 eligible nodes) would shift the root cause from resource exhaustion to a configuration drift, even if the scheduling error message looks the same.
A passing run of remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime while remote-agent-create fails would suggest the issue is isolated to the create path rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem.

Presence of no-history data (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) means we cannot confirm this is a regression; if historical runs are found to have been passing recently, that would strengthen the exhaustion hypothesis and help bound when capacity was consumed.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs Allocated ratio on eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.
Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned pods or VM allocations from prior probe runs remain after each observability run cycle.

Add a node-affinity-health eval that confirms the expected number of nodes (currently 2) carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and are in a Ready state, catching node label drift or node loss before it blocks agent provisioning.

Once historical run data is available, add a regression gate that fails the remote-agent feature check if it has not passed within the last N minutes, surfacing sustained outages more prominently than a single-run failure.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T04:45–04:50Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, no agent was created, and the remote-agent-state eval produced zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), failing its expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent eval pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–149 seconds before the eval timed out. This prevented agent creation entirely, so the remote-agent-state probe never reached the state-polling step and produced no evidence, causing a full contract gap (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all absent). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: [Highest confidence] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata peer-pods nodes are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for the eval pod.
[High confidence] Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool size: only 2 of 6 nodes carry this resource, and neither has spare capacity; the pool may need scaling or additional nodes.

[Medium confidence] Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable surface to only the 2 kata nodes. If the selector is overly restrictive or a node label was removed, the effective pool is smaller than intended.

[Low confidence] Concurrent workload contention: other pods may have consumed all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots just before the eval run, causing a transient exhaustion rather than a persistent capacity deficit. The simultaneous failure of all three sibling checks within the same ~5-minute window is consistent with a sustained exhaustion event rather than a brief spike.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place new agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner never received a running agent, and zero evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) were returned, causing a complete contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~144–149 s), preventing the eval from reaching the agent creation, state-polling, or runtime-chat stages. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint localized to the remote-agents Kubernetes node pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or a user-facing product outage (no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence).

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner could not collect any of the required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that advertise it. When the eval runner called createAgent with machineType "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1764), the resulting pod could not be scheduled: 2 nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption was also unavailable. The pod remained unscheduled for ~149 s until the eval timed out, producing an empty evidence object and failing all four required-evidence assertions (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState).

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on both eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs consumed all available VM slots and they have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry (the kata peerpods nodes), and those 2 nodes are at capacity — any change to node labels, taints, or the pod's affinity spec could cause this split.

Cluster under-provisioned for the remote-agent workload: only 2 nodes are configured to support kata.peerpods.io/vm, which may be insufficient if multiple concurrent eval runs or user workloads compete for the same resource.

Leaked or zombie VM allocations from previous eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if prior probe runs failed before cleanup executed, their VM slots may still be held, reducing available capacity.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of remote-agent-create that produces a scheduled pod and returns vmIdPresent=true and a valid remoteState would disprove that the resource is currently exhausted.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable > 0 and no pods currently consuming those slots would suggest the failure was transient (e.g., a brief spike) rather than sustained exhaustion.

Evidence that the pod's node affinity/selector was misconfigured (e.g., a label change on the 2 eligible nodes) would shift the root cause from resource exhaustion to a configuration drift, even if the scheduling error message looks the same.
A passing run of remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime while remote-agent-create fails would suggest the issue is isolated to the create path rather than a cluster-wide capacity problem.

Presence of no-history data (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) means we cannot confirm this is a regression; if historical runs are found to have been passing recently, that would strengthen the exhaustion hypothesis and help bound when capacity was consumed.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm Allocatable vs Allocated ratio on eligible nodes and warns when available slots fall below a minimum threshold, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.
Add a remote-agent-cleanup eval that verifies no orphaned pods or VM allocations from prior probe runs remain after each observability run cycle.

Add a node-affinity-health eval that confirms the expected number of nodes (currently 2) carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm label and are in a Ready state, catching node label drift or node loss before it blocks agent provisioning.

Once historical run data is available, add a regression gate that fails the remote-agent feature check if it has not passed within the last N minutes, surfacing sustained outages more prominently than a single-run failure.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-06-18T04:45–04:50Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are exhausted, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent eval pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With no schedulable node and no preemption victims available, the pod remained Unschedulable for ~144–149 seconds before the eval timed out. This prevented agent creation entirely, so the remote-agent-state probe never reached the state-polling step and produced no evidence, causing a full contract gap (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all absent). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Supported by the explicit 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' message in all three sibling check failures (failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, meaning the effective scheduling pool is already constrained to 2 nodes before resource limits are applied. If the selector was recently tightened or nodes were relabeled, capacity headroom would shrink. No source change evidence directly supports this, but the 4-node exclusion amplifies the impact of any VM resource pressure.

TERTIARY — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs not cleaned up by withCleanup: if cleanup failed on previous runs, VM slots may remain occupied. The eval runner uses withCleanup (run-status-probes.mjs:1795) but no evidence confirms prior cleanup succeeded (verifierContext.history.previousRunCount=0 means no prior run history is available to this packet).

LOWER — transient cluster event (node maintenance, eviction storm, scale-down): a temporary reduction in available kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes could produce this pattern without a persistent capacity problem. Would be disproved by a successful re-run shortly after.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful re-run of the remote-agent-runtime eval shortly after this failure with all 5 required evidence fields present would indicate a transient scheduling blip rather than sustained resource exhaustion.

Cluster node inspection showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are not fully allocated on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove the resource exhaustion hypothesis and point instead to a scheduler configuration or quota bug.

Evidence that the 4 nodes excluded by affinity/selector were previously included (e.g., a node label change or pod spec affinity change) would shift the primary cause to a configuration drift rather than capacity exhaustion.
Confirmation that all prior eval run cleanup (withCleanup) succeeded and no zombie pods are holding VM slots would rule out the leaked-pod hypothesis.

A passing run of remote-agent-create or remote-agent-state in the same time window would disprove the cluster-wide scheduling failure and localize the issue to a specific pod spec or timing condition.
